why_relevant: Publishes detailed local explainers and executive interviews on the acquiring/interchange dispute between retail and banks, and on processors such as UkrCard. High editorial standard; frequently the origin of figures other outlets recycle.
News agency running long-form interviews with the NBU governor and senior bankers where payment-market and cash-circulation policy detail surfaces; agency framing makes quotes citable.
Mainstream business desk with operational coverage of the banking and capital markets; secondary confirmation layer and occasional executive interviews touching cashless/card topics.

Publishes uk-language infographic write-ups of NBU card/ATM statistics ('Скільки в Україні платіжних карток і банкоматів'), making it a convenient structured restatement layer for the same underlying NBU series.

Smaller uk-language fintech/analytics outlet publishing structured digests of NBU payment-system reports (e.g. H1 2025 payment-system statistics from operations to innovations) — a lower-profile but topically precise source for this cell.

Data-explainer site that converts Ukrainian payment-infrastructure statistics into short quantified notes (e.g. +19% growth in card-accepting points in 2025). Low institutional weight but useful for surfacing series and framing; must be traced to primary.

Financial news aggregator that carried bank capex detail directly relevant to ATM fleets (PrivatBank buying 1,200 ATMs for UAH 1bn in 2025, with further purchases planned) — the kind of hardware-procurement datapoint rarely present in regulator statistics.

source_name: EMA Association (Українська міжбанківська асоціація членів платіжних систем ЄМА)
why_relevant: Interbank payment-systems association since 1999; runs recurring business events where it shares aggregated expert statistical and analytical information on payment and credit technologies and fraud. Its member list, event agendas and speaker rosters are a high-yield pointer to bank/PSP executives and to trade-press coverage of their numbers.

Domestic processor that indexes its own executives' media interviews ('ми у ЗМІ'), including a Forbes Ukraine interview with card-market and transfer-volume detail. A compact map of where processor executives speak and what numbers they release.

Bank press centre that explicitly publishes analytics and commentary from bank leadership on the Ukrainian financial market, including acquiring explainers. Useful as the upstream of many trade-press executive quotes in this cell, and PUMB is among the first banks authorised for non-financial payment services / open banking.

Ukrainian-language finance portal with news, advice and analytics on banks and personal finance; low institutional weight but occasionally surfaces retail-level card/cash behaviour framing. Monitor at low frequency.

Corporate content hub publishing uk-language merchant-side explainers on acquiring and payment acceptance; reveals how POS acceptance is marketed to Ukrainian SMEs and occasionally cites market sizing.

Mass-audience outlet that has run 'картки vs кеш' pieces on why Ukrainians are reluctant to abandon cash, typically citing association/bank research. Weak as evidence, useful for tracking public narrative on cash usage.

source_name: bne IntelliNews — Ukraine banking & finance coverage
why_relevant: Specialist emerging-Europe business newswire with sustained, numerate coverage of Ukrainian bank lending, deposits, cash withdrawals by firms, state-bank privatisation and NBU statistics; frequently the first English rendering of NBU/Ukrainian-language data releases.

Ukrainian news agency publishing in EN; carries NBU cashless/card statistics releases in near-real time and is used as a feed by Reuters and Bloomberg — a reliable English mirror of primary Ukrainian statistical announcements.

English-language Ukrainian outlet producing explanatory pieces on foreign fintech entries into Ukrainian banking (ZEN.com/PINbank, Iute/RwS Bank, Crédit Agricole/Bank Lviv) and wartime cash dynamics — good for market-entry and M&A signal.
Oldest English-language Ukrainian newspaper; business desk and expert opinion pieces on banking-sector stability, liquidity, and payments infrastructure resilience.
Reader-funded English-language Ukrainian outlet with a business desk; covers macro-financial policy, sanctions and bank-related developments that international readers act on.

source_name: The New Voice of Ukraine (english.nv.ua) — Business
why_relevant: English edition of NV; reports operational payments incidents (e.g. Mastercard outage disrupting cashless payments nationwide) and bank/market news that rarely reaches global wires.

Global fintech trade press carrying vendor and scheme announcements involving Ukraine (Mastercard Digital Country partnership, Mastercard+PrivatBank agentic payment, scheme blockades) — the clearest channel for cross-border/scheme-level developments.

source_name: The Paypers — Ukraine regulation & open banking
why_relevant: Payments-industry publication with interview-depth coverage of Ukrainian open banking (PSD2-aligned NBU model) and the Association of Ukrainian Banks — rare English primary-voice material on payments regulation.

Niche outlet tracking public-sector fintech; covers Ukrainian government MoUs with card schemes and Ministry of Digital Transformation payment initiatives — signals of state-driven payment digitalisation.

Cash-industry think tank publishing recurring English analyses of Ukrainian cash in circulation growth, ATM/branch counts, POWER BANKING resilience network and wartime withdrawal limits — directly on-topic for cash usage and ATM data.

source_name: European Payments Council — insights on NBU wartime payments
why_relevant: EU payments body publishing long-form insight pieces on how the NBU kept payments running in wartime; authoritative European framing of Ukrainian payment-system integration (SEPA context).

source_name: NBU English newsroom & Cashless Payments statistics pages
why_relevant: Primary regulator publishing its card/cashless/ATM/POS statistics and press releases in English — the anchor against which all foreign-media figures in this cell must be triangulated. Included here as the reference baseline for the EN channel.
Wire-style English coverage restating NBU non-cash payment details quickly; useful as a redundancy channel when Interfax is paywalled.
English feed of a Ukrainian agency reporting card-transaction share and cash withdrawal totals; complements the wire redundancy set for statistic-release detection.
